html:
The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 was a thirteen day standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union over Soviet nuclear missiles placed in Cuba. It was the closest the world has come to nuclear war.

After the Bay of Pigs, Nikita Khrushchev secretly sent missiles that could reach most of the United States. US spy planes found them. Kennedy declared a naval quarantine of Cuba, and the two powers came to the brink.

Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles in return for a US promise not to invade Cuba and a secret pledge to withdraw US missiles from Turkey. Castro was not consulted. The crisis led to a hotline between Washington and Moscow and to the first treaties limiting nuclear tests in the Cold War.
sum: The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 was a thirteen day standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union over Soviet nuclear missiles placed in Cuba. It was the closest the world has come to nuclear war.
